rule: good. context only and never parsed; the three texts carry the content that reaches the knowledge base.
texts: bad: "dim lanterns" comes out as a claim that the whole set of lanterns is dim rather than that each lantern is dim — a property of the collection, not of its members — and "toward" has no settled destination role, so that link is guessed. Rewrite as: "When a sky-cat hunts at a lantern-row, each nightmoth that survives the hunt flees to a dim lantern." — a singular indefinite lets "dim" attach to the lantern itself, "each" makes the per-moth reading explicit, and "to" is the destination preposition the translator has a rule for.
good. the surviving-nightmoth restriction lands in the rule's conditions and the move is minted per hunt, with "the Hollows" kept as a plain name and "to the Hollows" as the destination.

mixed: the rule fires and the content is all there, but the parse dropped the "a nightmoth is a moth" link that it emits in every other text of this item — a translator slip your wording did not cause, so no rewrite fixes it. The one wording-caused residue is that "the lanterns ... gain" reaches only the set as a whole, with no licensed way inside a rule to give each lantern its own threads; if you need the per-lantern reading, write "When a nightmoth flees and reaches the Hollows, each lantern at the Hollows gains silken threads."
